transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-15 16:00 UTC | Duration 62 mins | Recording available
Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Tom Nguyen (Redwood CSM); Liam O'Leary (NectarWorks Head of ML), Sofia Martinez (Platform Eng), Ravi Patel (CISO), Asha Verma (SRE)

[00:00] Jared: okay hey everyone thanks for carving out time today um it's a quick check-in ahead of your renewal window to go over the commitment refresh and the APAC onramp plan
[00:09] Liam: yeah thanks Jared we appreciate it, quick context — we've got about 3 months left on the current retainer and usage is trending up, especially chat features for support triage, so looking at both capacity and region add-ons
[00:22] Sofia: our production p95 for chat is hovering around 920ms right now, on average, which is okay for US users but we need mid 300s for APAC targets; we want to understand if that's realistic with Redwood hosted or if we need dedicated/apac-edge pods
[00:38] Priya: got it, thanks. quick clarifying q, are you currently sending requests through a us-west proxy, or do you have any egress points in asia?
[00:47] Asha: currently all egress is through gcp-us-west1, no apac egress. we're open to either using Redwood hosted apac region or spinning up dedicated capacity in ap-east if it's worth the delta
[01:03] Tom: just to add from an ops perspective, we saw spikes during product launches — concurrency can jump 6x for about 20 minutes, that burst behavior is a driver for the burst capacity ask
[01:15] Jared: okay makes sense. high level options: 1) hosted APAC region (fastest onboarding) 2) dedicated reserved capacity in APAC with guaranteed throughput 3) private/VPC deployment on your cloud in APAC. Each has tradeoffs on cost/latency/isolation
[01:31] Ravi: security first question — for option 3 we need KMS/HSM integration and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. also SOC2 attestation and ISO notes are table stakes — can you confirm those?
[01:44] Priya: yes, we have SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 in our security pack, we can share the package. for KMS integration, Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS and HSM — there are a couple of patterns, KMS proxied vs in-cloud CMK. we'll send the integration checklist
[02:04] Liam: sweet — also on quality, our prompts have long contexts (2k-3k tokens) and we rely heavily on KV cache reuse; any caveats on cache behavior across regions?
[02:14] Priya: good point. cross-region cache warming can increase latency if we don't colocate the KV cache. in hosted apac we keep cache local to the serving pool; if you go private with multi-region we can enable prefix caching and sticky routing but it needs config, there's a cost tradeoff
[02:32] Sofia: mhm okay. can you give a sense of numbers — like p95 delta if we stick with hosted us-west vs apac-hosted vs dedicated apac?
[02:41] Priya: ballpark: from us-west to apac routing adds 200-400ms network RTT depending on carrier. apac-hosted should get you p95 down to 300-500ms depending on model size and batching; dedicated apac can push p95 lower by another ~100-200ms because of tuned batching and local KV cache. caveat: quantization/profile and sequence length affect token time
[03:05] Jared: and cost wise, dedicated is a premium — predictable monthly fee plus commit, hosted is pay-as-you-go with some regional premiums for APAC instances. we can run a cost model once we know expected token volume and concurrency
[03:18] Liam: okay, that leads to commitment question — we were thinking of a modest uplift, not full reserved capacity right away. what's the smallest reserved increment?
[03:26] Tom: smallest reserved node pool is equivalent to 4x 80GB GPU capacity units for inference throughput, but we can structure a blended commit with burst credits; we proposed a stepped commitment last quarter
[03:38] Ravi: and SLA? if we move to dedicated, what's the p99 or availability SLA? we need guarantees for production SLAs with financial remedies
[03:46] Jared: for dedicated customers we provide an SLA in the contract appendix. p99 latency SLOs are part of the tuning but availability SLA is 99.9% with credits per incident — we'll share the exact language in the proposal
[03:58] [04:00] Sofia: unrelated but curious — competitors like Vertex have a per-instance autoscale granularity that's a bit cheaper for small bursts. how do you compare?
[04:09] Jared: we benchmarked against Vertex and Anthropic for similar workloads; Redwood focuses on KV caching and continuous batching to keep per-token cost down, and our Observe console gives better per-route token breakdowns for optimization. still, price parity varies by model and region
[04:25] [04:30] Priya: back to benchmarks — can you share a representative workload? ideally we'll run your top-10 prompts with typical concurrency, sequence lengths, and we will return p50/p95/p99 and throughput numbers
[04:41] Liam: yes, we'll prepare that. note some prompts include functions/tool-calls and streaming responses which change the token emission pattern
[04:50] Priya: noted — streaming adds a small overhead but often improves perceived latency; we'll include examples in the benchmark template
[05:01] Asha: on the security front, can you explain audit log retention and whether we can push logs to our S3 in region? we have compliance requirements for 7 years for certain events
[05:12] Tom: Redwood can export audit logs to customer destinations; retention policies are configurable in the enterprise package. long-term archival to your S3 is supported via log-export jobs, we'll confirm retention TTLs and costs
[05:27] Ravi: and encryption at rest — if we're doing private on-prem or VPC, we need HSM-managed keys and a key rotation policy we can control
[05:36] Priya: yes HSM integration is supported; if you go private we can broker HSM and you control rotation via your KMS. we'll include an integration flow diagram in the package
[05:46] [06:00] Jared: let's talk timeline: you mentioned wanting an APAC pilot in early May — what's the internal decision cadence?
[06:09] Liam: v1 decision by April 30 for pilot go-ahead, final contract by mid-May. stakeholders: Ravi for security sign-off, Sofia + Asha for ops, and me for budget.
[06:21] Jared: understood. we'll target those dates. Priya will run the benchmark this week and share results; I'll send revised pricing and a stepped commit proposal that includes a small reserved block + burst credits
[06:33] [06:45] Priya: quick note on batching/cost: aggressive batching reduces per-token cost but can increase tail latency under low concurrency; for chat you probably want conservative batching and prefix caching to preserve latency SLOs
[06:58] Sofia: that's the key tradeoff we care about — latency vs unit cost. we prefer to optimize for p95 first, then look at cost after pilot
[07:07] Priya: makes sense. we'll surface a few config profiles: low-latency (smaller batch sizes, more capacity), cost-optimized (larger batches, cache hits) and hybrid
[07:18] [07:30] Jared: on pricing structure, we can do blended rates across regions for the initial period or separate APAC pricing; blended simplifies invoicing, separate gives clearer unit economics. which do you prefer?
[07:40] Liam: keep billing simple for pilot, blended is fine. if we scale we'll move to separate region-specific commits
[07:49] Ravi: compliance Q - whats the log access cadence for auditors? we may need read-only access for third-party audits
[07:56] Tom: we can provide an audit view with read-only access scoped to the auditor's account and time window; we also provide signed attestations and evidence in the security package
[08:08] [08:30] Priya: ok i'm going to call out benchmark specifics: we'll measure p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, tokens/call, and KV hit rates, run 3 load profiles (steady, bursty, ramp). raw logs and perf traces will be shared in a drive link
[08:45] Sofia: perfect — we'll prepare sample prompts and traffic patterns. also note we sometimes use 8k context windows in experiments, that's not production but we want to see behavior
[08:55] Priya: fine we'll include a spot-check for 8k contexts but baseline for the pilot should be your 2-3k token windows
[09:05] [09:30] Ravi: last contract question: what flexibility for scaling mid-term? if our usage doubles do we get priority provisioning or do you require a 30-day lead?
[09:40] Jared: we provide burst provisioning and priority queueing for customers that have reserved capacity; without a commit we can still provide burst but lead times are longer. in the stepped commit we can include burst credits to cover short-notice spikes
[09:55] Asha: and how does failover work if a region goes down? we'd want automated fallback to US region with graceful degradation
[10:03] Priya: Redwood supports policy-based routing. you can set failover to a compatible model in another region — response latency will increase but service stays online. we can demo the failover behavior during the pilot
[10:16] Liam: okay great. are there any gotchas around model variants? we use a mix of flan-style instruction models and LLM-chat tuned ones
[10:24] Priya: model variants are supported; we recommend pinning a primary model and having a lighter fallback for capacity constrained periods. fallback mapping is part of rollout policy
[10:33] Jared: all right i think we have enough to action. quick recap: Redwood sends updated pricing + stepped commit proposal, Priya runs benchmark and shares results, security package and KMS checklist to Ravi, and NectarWorks prepares prompt set and traffic spreadsheet
[10:51] Liam: yep agreed. one more ask — can you include a sample runbook for pilot failover and for incident response? our SREs want that for the internal runbook review
[11:00] Tom: yes we have a standard pilot runbook and incident playbook, will attach to the proposal
[11:10] [11:30] Priya: any other technical concerns we should capture now?
[11:37] Sofia: nothing major, just want to validate p95 numbers and ensure KV caching behavior matches assumptions
[11:43] Ravi: security items covered. we'll review the package when it's in.
[11:49] Jared: great. we'll follow up with the artifacts. thanks everyone — we'll aim to get the benchmark & pricing out within the timelines discussed
[11:58] Liam: thanks all, look forward to the readout.
[12:05] Meeting ends

Shared links mentioned: [1] Security package (redwood/security/soc2_iso_packet_v2.pdf)  [2] APAC readiness checklist (redwood/internal/apac-onramp-checklist.docx)  [3] Benchmark template (drive/redwood/nectar-benchmark-template.xlsx)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings ("KV cash" vs "KV cache"), acronyms sometimes expanded incorrectly (SAML heard as "sample").
